fr.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches and shrubs along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Cut back vegetation at the driveway entrance to give arriving responders a clear line of sight onto the property.
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so it remains passable for emergency vehicles at all times.
• Thin dense vegetation along the access drive to reduce the risk of it closing off the only entry and exit point during an emergency.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees near the structure so fire cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Cut back shrubs and ground vegetation growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees across the property so there is clear open ground between individual trees and the structure.
• Trim branches and shrubs along both sides of the driveway so a fire vehicle can pass through without vegetation touching the vehicle.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches from the tree line to the road.
• Cut back ground vegetation along the driveway edges to reduce the amount of burnable material lining the route.
• Clear vegetation and debris from the limited turnaround area so fire vehicles can enter, turn, and exit without obstruction.
• Widen the usable turning space near the structure by removing shrubs or small trees that are reducing the open area.
• Separate mixed shrubs and trees near the structure so there are visible gaps between plant groupings rather than a continuous wall of vegetation.
• Remove dead branches, dry grass, and leaf litter from the ground beneath large trees near the structure.
• Maintain the single access route year-round by trimming any vegetation that grows back into the driveway corridor after seasonal growth.
